cards.title: Power Looks Good
cards.instruction: Act fascinated by confident behavior; imitate it closely while resenting how naturally it seems to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That pause of yours made everyone listen. I'll use a longer one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a cough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An authoritative cough. Mine will be deliberate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need to copy me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say that again. I like the certainty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your pause silenced the committee. I'll copy it for my report. Annoying how easily that works for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was holding back a cough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even your cough commands respect. How long did you hold it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just say, 'I'd like your attention.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like your attention. Was that your exact tone? You make four words look hereditary.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies the pause and A5 admires certainty, but neither expresses resentment at B's effortless success.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 converts B2's cough into authority; A5 starts copying the certainty of B4's objection.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects A's interpretation and B4 asks not to be copied, giving B an independent boundary.

heightening.evidence: A5 extends imitation from B's cough to B4's attempt to stop the imitation.

specificity.evidence: A1 mentions making everyone listen but leaves the occasion and A's next speaking task unclear.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'authoritative cough' and A5's request to repeat the objection are compact consequences of fascination.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 admires and resents the commanding pause; A3 studies its duration; A5 copies B's words and envies the apparently inherited tone.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's cough becomes A3's model of authority; B4's suggested sentence becomes A5's exact rehearsal.

relationship.evidence: B2 punctures A's interpretation and B4 offers practical help, although B's own committee responsibility remains unspecified.

heightening.evidence: After B4 simplifies the task, A5 makes even four ordinary words evidence of B's inaccessible natural advantage.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a committee report and an observed pause; A5 supplies immediately playable vocal imitation.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's commanding cough and A5's 'hereditary' delivery follow A's envy, though A1 states the attitude explicitly.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 reveals a suppressed cough; A3 interprets that specific involuntary behavior as another technique worth copying.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 supplies the attention request; A5 repeats it and checks the exact tone.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 combine fascination, close imitation and resentment of B's ease.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: B4's helpful simplification increases A5's conviction that even elementary speech comes naturally only to B.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A studies and closely copies B's apparently effortless confidence while begrudging B that ease.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Competitive imitation alone: original A1 wants a longer pause, but A3 and A5 show admiration without the required resentment.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A1 explicitly resents B's ease; A3 studies the cough and A5 copies B4's precise wording and tone.

records.recommendedEdit: The original omits part of the instruction. The revision introduces a committee report as an illustrative setting. records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a uses a colleague's verbal coaching; b uses physical imitation while a dining companion needs to leave.

cards.title: Power Looks Good
cards.instruction: Act fascinated by confident behavior; imitate it closely while resenting how naturally it seems to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got the table just by raising an eyebrow. Must be nice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could ask the waiter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I'm developing a stronger eyebrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's coming over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Watch mine outperform yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got us this table with one raised eyebrow. Show me. Must be nice having that face.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I raised the left one. But please just ask for the bill; I'm late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Left. Like this? You barely moved yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's coming. Keep it there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got a table in a second. I'm getting a cramp asking for paper.

heightening.evidence: A5 promises that the eyebrow will outperform B's, largely repeating A3's stronger-eyebrow ambition.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a restaurant table and an observable gesture that actors can immediately play.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'developing a stronger eyebrow' is concise and follows A1's misplaced admiration.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 contrasts a table gained instantly with a cramp over the bill; 'paper' is slightly less natural than the earlier wording.

cards.title: Only You Can Know
cards.instruction: Treat one person as the only safe place for your honest reactions, while hiding how much their discretion determines what you can risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Close the office door. You're the only person getting this version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could tell the team.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They can have the weather. This needs your discretion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's wrong?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me hear the latch first, then I'll stop editing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Close the office door. I hated the director's presentation. You're the only person I can say that to.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He asked me to collect feedback.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me down as engaged. This is just us having coffee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave your comments out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. The standing ovation felt like a hostage video. More coffee?

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 explicitly demands discretion; A5 openly makes honesty conditional on the latch, exposing the dependence A should hide.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's team suggestion, but A5 returns to A1's door without materially using B4's question.

relationship.evidence: B2 suggests another audience; B4 merely asks what is wrong and supplies no personal stake.

heightening.evidence: A5 repeats A1's request for privacy without increasing the risk or revealing an honest reaction.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an office and team, but A3 and A5 never identify what A needs to discuss.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's weather contrast is economical, while A5's 'stop editing' keeps the scene abstract.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 singles out B as the sole confidant; A3 disguises exposure as coffee, and A5 casually resumes honesty after reassurance.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's feedback role causes A3's public/private distinction; B4's promise permits A5's sharper criticism.

relationship.evidence: B2 has a real reporting responsibility; B4 chooses to protect A, though that choice comes readily.

heightening.evidence: After B4 promises omission, A5 risks the more pointed 'hostage video' comparison.

specificity.evidence: A1's office door and director's presentation establish an immediately playable confidential workplace exchange.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'engaged' euphemism and A5's coffee offer economically conceal the importance of B's discretion.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 reveals an official feedback channel; A3 supplies a safe official description and labels the rest private.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 removes the reporting risk, enabling A5 to disclose a harsher honest reaction.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1 identifies the sole safe person; A3 and A5 hide dependence on that safety beneath casual coffee talk.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 increases candor precisely when B4 guarantees discretion.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A reserves honest reactions for one trusted person while disguising how that person's discretion controls the risks A takes.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Ordinary confidentiality asks openly for secrecy without concealing emotional or practical dependence on the listener.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 supplies safe official feedback after B2 reveals a reporting role; B4's assurance releases A5's sharper honesty beneath casual hospitality.

records.recommendedEdit: The original exposed the dependence and stalled at B4. The revision keeps the office and introduces director feedback. Internal reread: cardFidelity 5, responseLogic 5, relationship 4, heightening 4, specificity 5, brevityWit 4; total 92. A3 masks the risk B2 creates, and B4's omission promise enables A5's stronger reaction. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; textual gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: B4 grants protection without much competing pressure. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A1 explicitly names the exclusive confidant; the concealment depends on playing A3 and A5's casual diversions sincerely.
records.alternativeComparison: The office alternative manages official reporting; the notebook alternative hides family disloyalty through self-deprecation.

cards.title: Only You Can Know
cards.instruction: Treat one person as the only safe place for your honest reactions, while hiding how much their discretion determines what you can risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wrote the truth in this notebook. Only you can read it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need to trust just me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'm simply starting with the entire current list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you tell anyone else?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After I know what honesty sounds like in a safe room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're the only one who's read my notebook. I don't want to take over Dad's shop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He wants me to bring it to Sunday lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the accounts notebook. This one's mostly spelling mistakes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll keep this one here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could I add something? I was relieved when the freezer broke. Terrible spelling on that page.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 restricts the notebook to B, but A5 directly announces the need for a safe room instead of hiding its importance.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's wider-trust suggestion, and A5 gives a condition in response to B4's question about others.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 both ask A to consider other confidants without establishing B's own interest.

heightening.evidence: A5 restates the exclusive safety already established by A1 rather than developing a concrete risk.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies a notebook, but A3 and A5 leave its truth and the relationship unidentified.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'entire current list' is compact wit; A5's abstract formulation sounds composed rather than immediate.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes B the notebook's exclusive reader; A3 and A5 camouflage consequential admissions as spelling mistakes.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's lunch request causes A3's notebook substitution; B4's safekeeping enables A5's additional confession.

relationship.evidence: B2 carries Dad's request and B4 protects A against it, establishing divided family obligations.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves beyond rejecting succession to admitting relief at a setback to Dad's shop after B4 secures the notebook.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes Dad's shop and a private notebook; B2's unspecified 'it' leaves Dad's knowledge slightly uncertain.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's spelling excuse returns in A5 as a compact cover for the more troubling freezer admission.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 threatens to bring the private notebook to Dad; A3 redirects the request to the accounts notebook.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 promises to retain the private notebook, giving A5 sufficient safety to add a worse admission.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A's exclusive trust in B drives disclosure, while the spelling pretext conceals its emotional stakes.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 deepens the family confession while maintaining A3's trivializing disguise.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A limits honest reactions to one confidant and minimizes the significance of the protection that makes those reactions possible.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Fear of disclosure alone would explain hiding the notebook but would not require disguising dependence on this particular person.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 calls consequential private writing spelling mistakes; B4's safekeeping then permits A5 to add a more compromising admission under the same cover.

records.recommendedEdit: The original lacked a concrete risk and disclosed its safety requirement. The revision introduces a family shop and Sunday lunch. Internal reread: cardFidelity 5, responseLogic 5, relationship 4, heightening 4, specificity 5, brevityWit 4; total 92. B2 threatens circulation, A3 substitutes notebooks, and B4's protection causes A5's further admission. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; textual gates pass.

cards.title: The Secrecy Protocol
cards.instruction: Treat concealment as a precise ritual with passwords, signals, approved phrases, and severe consequences for careless improvisation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Password before we discuss the sandwiches.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're in an empty kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nobody can interrupt the password.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is it still cucumber?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not aloud. You've triggered the vegetable-reset protocol.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write the password before I hand over the surprise picnic sandwiches.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're alone in the kitchen, and the bus leaves in two minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then write quickly. Speaking it cancels collection.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've written cucumber. That's yesterday's password, isn't it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've said it. The sandwiches stay here. I'll tell the walkers their lunch failed clearance.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 requires a password and A5 invokes a reset, but severe consequences remain unspecified and speaking the requested password becomes arbitrarily wrong.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's empty kitchen, but A5 penalizes B4 for saying the password A1 requested without establishing a silent method.

relationship.evidence: B2 questions the need and B4 tries to comply, giving A resistance followed by cooperation.

heightening.evidence: A5 escalates to a reset protocol, although the practical consequence is only a label.

specificity.evidence: A1's sandwiches and B2's empty kitchen create a clear mundane setting for excessive secrecy.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's uninterrupted password follows B2, while A5's vegetable protocol partly relies on decorative terminology.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 requires a written password, A3 specifies cancellation for speaking, and A5 enforces that consequence.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's two-minute deadline with faster compliance; A5 applies the spoken-password rule to B4's 'cucumber.'

relationship.evidence: B2 urgently needs lunch released before the bus; B4 attempts compliance while checking the outdated password.

heightening.evidence: A5 lets the entire group's lunch fail clearance rather than relax the ritual after B4's accidental breach.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies picnic sandwiches and B2 a departing bus; the precise surprise being protected is lightly defined.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'lunch failed clearance' follows the established cancellation rule and the walkers' practical need.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 argues solitude and urgency; A3 refuses relaxation and demands faster written compliance.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 says the password aloud, triggering the cancellation rule A3 has already stated.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A treats concealment as exact procedure with explicit penalties outweighing the picnic's practical purpose.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 enforces a group-level consequence; the refusal remains an in-scene obstacle B can contest, not a prescribed ending.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A makes concealment an exact ritual and treats departures from approved communication as grounds for disproportionate consequences.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Generic secret-agent play adds passwords as decoration; this card makes compliance determine concrete access and penalties.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 establishes that speaking cancels collection before B4 says the password, so A5's withheld lunch follows a stated rule.

records.recommendedEdit: The original password punishment lacked a prior rule. The revision retains kitchen sandwiches and adds a picnic departure. Internal reread: cardFidelity 5, responseLogic 5, relationship 4, heightening 5, specificity 5, brevityWit 4; total 95. B4's spoken password breaches A3's explicit restriction, causing A5's disproportionate cancellation. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; textual gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: The protected surprise is less concrete than the protocol, and cancellation is a strong beat, though it leaves bargaining available. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A5 announces a penalty rather than resolving the exchange; B can still bargain over the sandwiches and imminent bus.
records.alternativeComparison: This enforces a stated breach penalty under transport pressure; alternative b uses gestures and retraining to control access to candle duty.

cards.title: The Secrecy Protocol
cards.instruction: Treat concealment as a precise ritual with passwords, signals, approved phrases, and severe consequences for careless improvisation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Signal the cupboard with three fingers. Don't say where the cake is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake's on the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then use the table signal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Which is?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That information requires the cake briefing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Signal Mum's birthday cake location: three fingers for cupboard, four for fridge. Say it aloud and you're off the surprise team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the table. The helpers need to find it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're off. Table is a flat palm. I'll signal them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already sent them a photo. That doesn't say anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It shows everything. Now we move the cake and change the signals. You won't be told where your slice is.

hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1 establishes precise concealment rituals and a penalty; A3 enforces them sincerely; A5 expands the security response after another disclosure.

This correction retains Mum's birthday and exact location signals, replacing candles and the committee with helpers and a revealing photograph. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: cardFidelity 5, because A1 prescribes signals and exclusion, A3 enforces them, and A5 responds to unauthorized visual disclosure by relocating the secret and changing signals; responseLogic 5, because B2's spoken table location causes A3's penalty and flat-palm correction, while B4's photograph specifically causes A5's relocation and exclusion from the new location; relationship 4, because B2 needs helpers to find the cake and B4 defends a practical silent solution, which A treats as a breach; heightening 4, because A5 expands one helper's removal into disrupted preparations and withheld knowledge of B's own serving; specificity 4, because A1 establishes a family birthday and B2 a concrete delivery need, although the opening remains procedural; brevityWit 4, because B4's distinction between showing and saying drives A5's disproportionate secrecy around a single slice. cards.title: You Owe Me a Miracle
cards.instruction: Carry one past favor as sufficient reason to expect an impossible act in return, and present the exchange as perfectly fair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You owe me lunch money. Bring back ten minutes of yesterday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant I'd buy lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said anything. I kept the word.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't travel through time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll need to start earlier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I covered your lunch yesterday. Bring back the ten minutes I spent queuing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy your lunch today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That covers the sandwich. I'm only asking for my time back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can queue for you today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. Use that time to retrieve yesterday's minutes. Then we're square.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 responds to B2's limited offer; A5's 'start earlier' sidesteps B4's inability to travel through time.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers lunch and B4 states a limit, providing a credible debtor's resistance.

heightening.evidence: A5 supplies a time pun without increasing the repayment obligation or its practical consequences.

specificity.evidence: A1 names lunch money but gives no reason A wants those particular ten minutes of yesterday.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 is concise, while A5's detachable 'start earlier' joke weakens the exchange's specific logic.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes yesterday's lunch sufficient grounds for retrieving elapsed time; A5 presents that impossible repayment as settling accounts.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 distinguishes B2's sandwich repayment from lost time; A5 repurposes B4's queueing offer into time retrieval.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 offer increasingly relevant compensation, giving A actual solutions to reinterpret.

heightening.evidence: A5 recruits today's queueing into the demand, but mostly restates A1's unchanged ten-minute debt.

specificity.evidence: A1's lunch queue and ten minutes make the impossible claim concrete, though the present setting remains light.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's sandwich/time distinction is economical; A5's 'Then we're square' sustains the sincere fairness claim.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 offers lunch; A3 credits only the sandwich and keeps the elapsed-time debt outstanding.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 offers queueing time; A5 assigns that offered time to recovering yesterday's minutes.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A treats a modest favor as justification for an impossible but supposedly balanced repayment.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 converts a helpful offer into an assigned method of satisfying the original impossible debt.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A values a concrete past favor as sufficient payment for an impossible return and calmly treats that accounting as fair.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Enforcing an impossible promise would make B's wording the source of obligation instead of A's earlier kindness.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A3 relies on 'anything'; revised A3 divides the sandwich from the time debt and A5 calls impossible repayment square.

Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A1/A3 ground fairness in the favor), logic 5 (A3 uses lunch; A5 uses queueing), relationship 4 (B offers two remedies), heightening 4 (A5 assigns the remedy to impossible collection), specificity 5 (A1 identifies the lost minutes), brevity/wit 4 (A5's 'square' completes the accounting); total 92. cards.title: The Plan Gets Better
cards.instruction: Celebrate every setback as proof that the scheme is becoming more sophisticated, selective, or impossible to detect.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The alley's blocked. Excellent: our secret proposal picnic just got harder to discover.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better camouflage. Everyone will assume we're moving house.
